comment: 1. The forward-reference gate: each technical term names the chapter
that defines it. scripts/book-gates.ts fails the build when a
term's first occurrence in reading order lands before its defining
chapter. Matching is case-insensitive on word boundaries, over the
chapters' full text including code fences.
2. The reader-facing notation card, book/NOTATION.md, generated from
this file by scripts/gen-notation-card.ts. `say` is how to read the
term out loud; `gloss` is the one-line meaning; `symbol` is the
notation, where the term has one. Entries with a symbol are listed
first on the card, because a reader who stalls is usually stalling
An entry may set "gate": false to opt out of job 1 — only for
terms that are also ordinary English. It must then carry a
`gateNote` saying why, and the gate counts the exemptions out loud.
The gate checks that this file and the generated card agree, the same
way book/RULES.md is checked against book/rules.json.

kernel.gloss: The small component that checks proofs. The only part of a proof assistant that has to be correct.

environment.gloss: The map from names to already-checked declarations. It only ever grows, and a name may enter it once.

declaration.gloss: What the kernel is handed: a name, a stated type, and — for a definition — a value.

turnstile.say: in context gamma, e has type alpha
turnstile.gloss: The judgment the whole book computes. Γ (gamma) lists the variables in scope with their types; ⊢ is called a turnstile.

de Bruijn.gloss: A variable written as the number of binders between it and the binder it belongs to. #0 is the nearest.

bound variable.gloss: A variable introduced by a binder inside the term. Written as an index, never as a name.

free variable.gloss: A serial-numbered stand-in used while the checker works under a binder. Its type lives in a side table.

alpha-equivalence.gloss: Sameness up to renaming bound variables. With indices instead of names it costs nothing: equal terms are equal trees.

substitution.gloss: Replace the variable x by the term a throughout e, renumbering indices so nothing is captured.

universe ladder.gloss: The tower of universes. Sort 0 is Prop (propositions); Sort 1 is Type (data types); Sort (l+1) holds Sort l.

imax.gloss: The level of a function type. Collapses to 0 when the result is a proposition, however large the domain.

impredicativ.gloss: A proposition may quantify over all propositions and stay a proposition. True of Prop only; the data rungs are predicative.

reduces to.gloss: One computation step. The rules are beta, zeta, delta, iota, and the primitives of chapters 9 and 10.

weak head normal form.gloss: Reduce at the head until the head is a binder, a sort, or stuck — and stop. Never under a binder, never an argument.

whnf.gloss: The usual abbreviation for weak head normal form, and the name of the function that computes it.

beta.gloss: Apply a function: substitute the argument into the body.

delta.gloss: Unfold a constant that has a definition, substituting the use site's universe levels into its value.

zeta.gloss: Inline a let-bound name. A let is shared text, not an abstraction barrier.

definitionally equal.say: a is definitionally equal to b
definitionally equal.gloss: Equal up to computation. This is structural typing with programs inside the shapes, so deciding it means running them.

definitional equality.gloss: The relation above, as a noun. Sound but incomplete, and — because of proof irrelevance — not transitive.

proof irrelevance.gloss: Any two proofs of one proposition are definitionally equal. The source of both warts in the line above.

conversion rule.gloss: The typing rule that calls definitional equality: an argument's type must match the function's domain up to computation.

eta.gloss: A function equals its own one-step wrapper: f == fun x => f x. Chapter 7 adds the version for records.

inductive type.gloss: A data type declared by the input file: a name, some constructors, their types. The kernel reviews it before accepting.

telescope.gloss: A chain of binders where each type may mention the variables before it. A constructor's type is one.

parameter.gloss: An argument of the declared type that is fixed across every constructor — a list's element type, for instance.

positivity.gloss: The declared type may appear as the result of a constructor argument's type, never to the left of an arrow inside it.

subsingleton.gloss: A proposition with one constructor whose every field is forced by the result type. Nothing about it can vary.

projection.gloss: Field i of a structure value. Typed by walking the constructor's telescope; reduces only against a literal constructor application.

structure.gloss: A data type with exactly one constructor. Earns field access and two extra definitional equalities.
structure.gateNote: An ordinary English word as well as a technical one: chapter 5 says "union-find structure" in the everyday sense. The forward-reference gate cannot tell word senses apart, so this entry is card-only.

recursor.gloss: The constant the kernel gives back for a data type: `reduce` for that type, whose type is its induction principle.

motive.gloss: What the recursor is proving or building, as a family over the type and its indices.

minor premise.gloss: One per constructor: show the motive holds there, given it holds for every recursive argument.

major premise.gloss: The value actually being destructed — the last argument of the recursor.

iota.gloss: The recursor's computation rule: applied to a constructor, select that constructor's minor premise and recurse.

K-like.gloss: Fire iota on a subsingleton proof without inspecting it — guarded by a definitional-equality check that is itself a soundness rule.

quotient.gloss: The type where r-related elements are identified. Four kernel-built constants and one computation rule.

NDJSON.gloss: Newline-delimited JSON: the export format, one object per line, with growing tables of names, levels and expressions.

lean4export.gloss: The tool that writes a checked Lean library out in that format, including the githash of the kernel that checked it.
